According to Table 1 from the document "Perspectives on the relationship between materials chemistry and roll-to-roll electrode manufacturing for high-energy lithium-ion batteries" (ensm-2020), the technologies with the highest and the lowest upper bound of estimated energy density improvement are:

* The highest upper bound is 350 Wh/kg, which is achieved by combining the following approaches: all-water-based processing of layered Co-free cathodes such as LiNi0.8-Fe0.1Al0.1O2; thick, structured electrode architectures with graded pore and particle size distributions; processing of Co-free cathodes and graphite anodes with high-speed EB curing; complete elimination of formation cycling; and integration of these technologies with manufacturing of solid-state Li battery components.
* The lowest upper bound is 220-240 Wh/kg, which is achieved by Section 8 – Coating Parameter and Drying Protocols.

The upper bounds of estimated energy density improvement for these two technologies are 350 Wh/kg and 240 Wh/kg, respectively. Therefore, the upper bounds are 110 Wh/kg apart.
